page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6a.xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7H12 processor running at 2.6 GHz. The instance is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, providing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, and relies on a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates that the ecs.c6a.xlarge exhibits modest performance characteristics. In stress-ng CPU tests, both single-core and multi-core performance fall into the bottom 10%. Memory bandwidth tests, including large-block read and write operations, are positioned in the bottom 25%. However, the instance achieves average results in single-threaded gzip compression, single-threaded bzip3 decompression, and Geekbench single-core testing. Multi-threaded decompression and Geekbench multi-core scores remain in the bottom 10% and bottom 25% respectively, reflecting limitations in scaling parallel workloads.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.c6a.xlarge offers a dedicated hardware profile with a low resource footprint. The lack of bundled local storage and modest network bandwidth of 2 Gbps represent clear tradeoffs for resource-intensive applications. Given its average performance in single-threaded compression and text processing, but weaker results in database operations, redis SET operations, and static web serving, this instance is suited for lightweight compute tasks, basic text processing, and single-threaded utility workloads rather than high-throughput database or web serving environments.
